clause_evidence.clause: Determine the place value of a digit
clause_evidence.reasoning: Multiple samples directly ask students to identify or evaluate place value: sample 4 asks for place value of 2 in 20 (answer 20), sample 9 asks for place value of 1 in 15 (answer 10), sample 11 asks for place value of 1 in 12 (answer 10). These items consistently and correctly test place value determination across different two-digit numbers.

All 20 samples use 2-digit numbers exclusively. The numbers range from 10 to 97 (testing 10, 12, 15, 17, 19, 20, 40, 45, 50, 76, 85, 95, 97), ensuring comprehensive coverage within the required domain without exceeding two-digit bounds.

Samples test the value of digits in various positions. Sample 3 asserts value of 0 in ones place equals 0, sample 6 tests that value of 9 in tens place should be 90 (not 97), sample 17 tests that value of 9 in ones place should be 9 (not 90), and sample 18 confirms value of 5 in ones place equals 5. Students must understand that digit value depends on positional context.

Extensive coverage of digit identification appears across 13 samples that ask students to identify which digit occupies a specified place: samples 1, 8, 15, 19 identify ones digits; samples 13, 16, 20 identify tens digits; samples 2, 5, 7, 10, 12, 14 ask students to name the place occupied by a given digit across multiple formats.
